questions.question: In List<String> names = new ArrayList<>(), which part is the interface?
questions.explanation: The variable is declared against the List interface and refers to an ArrayList object.

questions.question: What does the String argument guarantee?
options: Elements added through this reference must be Strings
questions.explanation: The element type flows through generic method signatures.

questions.question: Which is a utility class containing static algorithms?
questions.explanation: Collection is an interface; Collections contains helpers such as sort and reverse.

questions.question: Why declare against List rather than ArrayList when possible?
options: Client code depends on the needed behaviour, not one implementation
questions.explanation: Programming to the interface reduces unnecessary coupling.
